What’s happening behind the captions?

A specialist visual speech model reads camera frames. An offline model repeatedly processes a growing window to produce drafts; this is not a fully streaming recognizer. Pauses, the sentence button, or an eight-second limit trigger a fuller decoder pass. A pause is estimated and can be misdetected. The studio overlay tracks four actual face landmarks; it is not a phoneme or confidence visualization.

Silent lip reading is ambiguous and cannot guarantee exact words. Optional context assistance selects among the visual model’s existing readings. It does not verify the words. Optional AI voice reads a predicted caption using generated speech. Only caption text is sent to your model when those features are used; camera frames stay on your computer. API usage is billed to the connected key.

Reviewed agent requests and tool receipts are saved locally in a private database. They can be cleared from the computer. Camera video stays in memory unless you press Record in Studio. Studio recordings contain the camera, caption provenance labels, and optional generated voice; they never contain microphone input. MP4 conversion uses temporary files on your computer that are deleted after conversion. Cloudflare relays the connection.
